en: By the rivers of Babylon,
there we sat, and we also wept,
when we remembered Zion.
On the willows [?] in its midst
we hung up our lyres.
For there our captors asked us for words of song,
and our tormentors [?] for joy:
"Sing us one of the songs of Zion."
How shall we sing the song of YHWH
on foreign soil?
If I forget you, Jerusalem,
let my right hand forget.
Let my tongue cling to my palate
if I do not remember you,
if I do not raise Jerusalem
above the head of my joy.
Remember, YHWH, against the sons of Edom
the day of Jerusalem,
those who said, "Lay it bare, lay it bare,
down to its foundation!"
Daughter of Babylon, you who are laid waste,
happy is he who repays you
the deed that you dealt to us.
Happy is he who seizes and dashes your little ones
against the rock.
notes: The divine name is written יְהֹוָה (the four letters YHWH with the vowels of Adonai, "Lord"); it is romanized and translated as YHWH. In reading it is said "Adonai".
Cantillation marks, the paseq (׀) and sof pasuq (׃) are not romanized; maqaf is shown as a hyphen.
line 2.1: 'aravim' is traditionally 'willows'; most botanists take it as the Euphrates poplar.
line 3.2: 'tolalenu' occurs only here; 'our tormentors' (or 'our plunderers') is the usual reading, but the sense is uncertain.
line 5.2: the Hebrew has no object: 'let my right hand forget [its skill]' or 'wither' (a common emendation) are both proposed.
line 8.1: 'hashshedudah' is 'the devastated one'; many read it as 'who is to be devastated'.
